intended_object: The comultiplication Δ : K^Γ → K^Γ ⊗_K K^Γ on the algebra of K-valued functions on a finite group Γ, dual to the group law: Δ(f)(g,h) = f(gh), under the identification K^Γ ⊗ K^Γ ≅ K^{Γ×Γ}. This is the coordinate-ring comultiplication of the constant group scheme (Milne, Algebraic Groups, 2.3). Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The body first builds the algebra map K^Γ → K^{Γ×Γ}, f ↦ ((g,h) ↦ f(g*h)), as `AlgHom.pi` of evaluations at `p.1 * p.2`. It then applies the inverse of `tensorAlgEquiv`. The lemma `tensorAlgEquiv_tmul_apply` shows that this equivalence sends x ⊗ y to (g,h) ↦ x g * y h. So Δ(f) is exactly the tensor whose value at (g,h) is f(gh); the lemma `tensorAlgEquiv_comulAlgHom_apply` states this. That is the standard formula Δ(δ_k) = Σ_{gh=k} δ_g ⊗ δ_h. The ingredients have the right generality: any commutative base ring K, and finiteness of Γ, which is needed for K^Γ ⊗ K^Γ ≅ K^{Γ×Γ}.

Strictly speaking, only `Mul` (or a monoid structure, for coassociativity and the counit) is used here, not inverses. But the definition belongs to the Hopf-algebra structure of a constant *group* scheme, whose antipode needs inverses. Taking `[Group Γ]` is the natural setting there and matches Milne, so I don't count it as too narrow.

Mathlib has no Hopf or coalgebra structure on the algebra of functions on a finite group; its `Bialgebra/MonoidAlgebra` is the dual, group-algebra side. So there is no Mathlib counterpart.
